detail: FOUND a verified national+regional non-renewal instrument with a defined denominator, closing part of the standing gap. Source: US Treasury FIO "Analyses of U.S. Homeowners Insurance Markets, 2018-2022: Climate-Related Risks and Other Factors" (published Jan 2025), built on the NAIC/FIO PCMI Data Call (80% of HO-3/HO-5 policies nationwide by premium, 45M+ policies/yr, 33,000+ ZIP codes). DEFINITION (verbatim, p.7): "Nonrenewal Rate = Count of Nonrenewals in Reporting Year / Policies in Force at End of Reporting Year". NATIONAL avg 2018-2022 = 1.04%; national annual trend flat 2018-19, dipped 2020-21 (COVID moratoria), rose to 1.20% in 2022. By NATIONAL TLCR (Top-Level Climate Risk) quintile 2018-2022 avg: Highest-Risk 1.61% vs Lowest-Risk 0.90% (a 0.71-pt spread); Highest-Risk rose 1.10%(2018) -> 2.37%(2022), more than doubling. SOUTHWEST region (CA/AZ/NV/CO/NM/UT - the wildfire-dominant HOI-peril region per this same report): regional avg 1.28% (23.5% above national), Highest-Risk category 1.92%, Higher-Risk 1.38%. NORTHWEST region (WA/OR/ID/MT/WY/AK - the OTHER wildfire-dominant region): regional avg 0.67% (35% BELOW national), Highest-Risk 0.86%, Higher-Risk 0.74%. TENSION FLAG for AEOLUS: the NW is where 2026's LIVE fire activity concentrates (OR 16/WA 16 large fires as of 8/27) but its 2018-2022 non-renewal baseline runs below the national average - the 2026 season postdates this dataset by 4+ years and cannot yet be read through it. REMAINING GAP: report explicitly EXCLUDES 2023 and 2024 data and states in its own limitations section that "public data suggests that premiums and nonrenewals" have likely continued rising since; no WA-STATE-specific (only regional) cut exists in this source; Texas insurer data is excluded from the nonrenewal calculation entirely (footnote, Figure 8). CA DOI FAIR Plan policy-in-force growth (a proxy, not a rate) was found via secondary search only (WebSearch summary, not a direct primary fetch) and is NOT logged as a fact here per hard limits - see RUN_REPORT gaps.
